title: Library limitations, merged and placed on the map
status: Map evidence. No fixes, no verdicts. Built by docs/program/evidence/library-pathways/build-limitations.js.txt.
how_to_read: Each item is one mechanism by which the library design falls short of its goal.
real.cases counts the walks (of 59) whose walker named this mechanism. real.families counts the ten pathway families those walks belong to.
The 59 real cases are a chosen sample of problem cases. A count shows that a route exists and where a step breaks. It never shows how often this happens.
Tag M: counted on this PC from the walk records. No number in this file is a rate.
contradicted lists families whose real cases showed the item did not happen or mattered less, with the cases on that side. The item stays in the list.
params are the map.json parameters through which the item acts in the model. An empty list means it acts through none.
merged_from counts the raw items absorbed: real-case breaks, plus titles from the two thought-experiment lists.
Items are sorted by main step, then by how many real cases showed them.
works lists places where the design worked or would have helped in a real case. Its figures (calls, days, messages) come from the walk records (tag M).

words.window: what a model can see while it works: the conversation, files read, notes loaded.
words.entry: one stored conclusion in the library.
words.tier: a model level on the ladder: Sonnet (cheap), Opus, Fable (top).
words.helper window: a short separate session (a subagent) started by a main session.
words.check: whatever decides a result is right: tests, a review, a build, a rerun.

counting.unit: one walk = one real case (59 in all).
counting.rule: A walk counts for an item when a break merged into the item names it in the *-walk.md Breaks section, or a quoted walk note shows it. Two items list an extra walk from a walk note.
counting.per_break_differences_note: L01 counts some breaks per case (C1 to C6) while its walks split cases (C1a, C1b ...). Where they differ, the walks whose notes show the break are counted.
same_incident_in_two_families: L03:C3, L02:C3 and L06:C2 (the WhatsApp dispatcher)

items.title: Short helper windows start without the session's lessons
items.what: Work is split across many short helper windows. Each starts fresh, so it must look up or relearn what the parent session already knew.

contradicted.reason: Helper windows in the same folder receive CLAUDE.md and the memory index at transcript line 6. They lack only what the session learned since the last memory write.
Fresh windows found every defect: the adversarial audit, the red team, the adversarial re-read, the root reviews. Emptiness was the asset here.
The copies were made in long main sessions (835 and 831 calls). Helper windows were reviewers, and they caught defects.
The review that refuted the wrong hypothesis was a fresh helper window told to refute. Its empty window was not anchored by the main session's guess.
Fresh Sonnet gatherers with a pointed brief found the withdrawal and summarised a 972-line design accurately.
The helper windows carried the shell rule in their briefs. The windows lacking cross-project knowledge were the long-lived Fable sessions.
MEMORY.md and CLAUDE.md sit at line 6 or 7 of every helper window checked (three sessions). Only index lines arrive; a note's body needs a read or a brief.

known_titles: 16 many short subagent windows start empty

works.text: A stored pdftoppm route served to the second wave would have saved 2 to 8 calls per agent across four Opus agents.
One git flag with an exact error template, served before cloning, would have saved the 15 failed clones of 11-04.
The pushed Python note worked at no extra cost: three agents carried its remedy in the same command as the probe, on 11-09 and 11-12.
The memory index put the long-paths fix into a sibling session before its first clone; that clone never failed.
A lookup by the failing test's name would have hit the root's entry, saving a wrong fixture commit, its revert, stopped runs and one Opus review.
The check held: an exact match to an old, fixed cause was tested, came back 'does not apply', and no wrong fix was applied.
After the first solve, a do-not-apply entry on the handoff's wrong advice stops a change that would let a 4-digit PIN be guessed without limit. CLAUDE.md already warns.
The action words 'enable dispatcher' reach the stored hazard, preventing the replay measured at 36 messages about months-old jobs, plus permanent suppressed rows.
The builder's own words 'offline presence outbox' reach the right entry; had a lookup fired, it saves three days of stuck badges and a rework commit.
A red check handed raw output to Fable, which fixed the defect in about a minute and wrote the rule, with its reason, within two minutes.
The S02 entry, fetched at the S04 check, would have stopped the top tier's wrong premise: one finding's round trip saved.
A later change reused two stored traps and avoided at least two failed cloud builds; a later design reused one that cost about 15M helper tokens.
A design 'no' stored with its reason held for five months and was never argued again.
The design's scan for fixes not on the main branch fits June exactly: it removes one of build 15's two causes and 16 days of broken main.
The empty-value check promoted into the shared test run blocks that mistake for every agent and human, with no lookup.
